findings.title: Salesforce service references Prisma without importing it
findings.body: This file now calls `prisma.credential.update(...)`, but its imports do not include `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. TypeScript compilation of the app-store package will fail with `Cannot find name 'prisma'`, preventing this change from building.

findings.title: The minimum sync response schema strips every expiry field
findings.body: The computed property names here are evaluated to the literal string `"[object Object]"`; they do not create dynamic Zod properties. The second duplicate property also overwrites the first, and `z.object()` strips all unrecognized fields by default. Consequently, when credential syncing is enabled, a normal sync response such as `{ access_token, expires_in }` is parsed down to only `access_token` (plus the synthetic refresh token). Callers such as the Zoom adapter then calculate an expiry using `newTokens.expires_in`, which is undefined, producing `NaN` and potentially failing the credential update; other adapters retain stale expiry values and repeatedly refresh.

findings.title: Google refresh stores the Zod safe-parse wrapper as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the full `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but this update stores that result itself as `credential.key` rather than `key.data`. This occurs for every Google token refresh, including when sync is disabled. On the next use, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives the wrapper instead of Google credentials and rejects it, leaving the user with an unusable Google Calendar connection.

findings.title: HubSpot treats a fetch Response from the sync endpoint as a HubSpot token
findings.body: The native HubSpot refresh API returns a token object directly, but `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch` `Response` whenever syncing is enabled. This code casts that Response to `HubspotToken` and immediately reads `expiresIn` and `accessToken`; both are undefined because the response body is never parsed. It then persists the Response-shaped object and sets the HubSpot client access token to undefined, so synced HubSpot credentials cannot refresh or create meetings.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential ID as the Cal user ID to the sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` expects its third argument to be the owning Cal user ID and serializes it as `calcomUserId`. This call passes `credentialId` instead. The external app store will therefore look up a user whose ID equals the database credential ID, usually returning no credential and, in the event of an ID collision, potentially returning another user's token.

findings.title: Webhook credential create/update is not atomic
findings.body: The handler performs `findFirst` followed by either `update` or `create`, with no transaction or uniqueness constraint. Concurrent deliveries for the same user and app can both observe no credential and create duplicates. Later deliveries update an arbitrary `findFirst` result while stale duplicate credentials remain eligible for use, so the app store can no longer reliably be the source of truth.
